history.title: One blower module, two chassis: the $1,300 step

style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Split-screen diptych, clean vertical seam down the middle, staged inside a garage on a weathered concrete floor. Left half: a compact tracked yard-robot chassis in matte graphite polymer, the 24-inch two-stage snow blower module latched on top, brushed-steel intake and raised discharge chute. Right half: the identical snow blower module latched onto a larger chassis with exposed brushless hub motors at each track. One directional key light raking from the upper left throws long cast shadows across the concrete; matte muted palette of graphite, bone white and a single ochre accent on the chute; moulding seams, contact shadows, hard clean edges, unlettered surfaces.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, logos
rationale: The story is a single number — the $1,300 chassis step — and a modularity fact: one blower, two bases. component_assembly is the treatment built for exactly that restraint, and the split-screen diptych makes the unchanged module and the differing chassis legible in a single glance at card size. It also rotates the desk away from the four photographic looks used most recently.
cue: Your Snow Cores Are $1,300 Apart, One Blower
subject: the identical 24-inch snow blower module mounted on two different tracked yard-robot chassis
core_thesis: Yarbo's $1,300 gap between the Y40 Core and Y40P Core snow bundles buys brushless hub motors and 1,000 extra square feet of range — never a bigger blower — so the mapped area, not the marketing, should pick the Core.
core_conflict: Identical snow-clearing hardware versus a $1,300 chassis premium: the same 24-inch two-stage module rides both Cores, and only the base unit — motors and range — sets the bill.
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast, identical blower module on each side of a clean vertical seam

review.depicts: A split-screen diptych showing a tracked yard-robot chassis fitted with a snow blower module (front auger and top discharge chute) photographed in a garage, with the left panel showing one chassis/top-unit configuration and the right panel showing a slightly different chassis configuration carrying the same blower module.
review.reason: The image literally shows the article's own mechanism — the identical snow blower module mounted on two different tracked robot base units in a left-right split — matching the headline's same-blower-different-base price story.

input.prompt:
Split-screen diptych, clean vertical seam down the middle, staged inside a garage on a weathered concrete floor. Left half: a compact tracked yard-robot chassis in matte graphite polymer, the 24-inch two-stage snow blower module latched on top, brushed-steel intake and raised discharge chute. Right half: the identical snow blower module latched onto a larger chassis with exposed brushless hub motors at each track. One directional key light raking from the upper left throws long cast shadows across the concrete; matte muted palette of graphite, bone white and a single ochre accent on the chute; moulding seams, contact shadows, hard clean edges, unlettered surfaces.

Do not include: people, faces, hands, garbled text, random lettering, numbers, signage, watermarks, UI, logos.
